integrity: The full primary proof was checked at the normalization, polar factor, entropy identity, Hardy--Bergman identity, strict kernel positivity, small-exponent kernel estimate, multiplicity approximation, and endpoint passages. Strictness for repeated roots is proved by a compact-interior lower bound that survives the source approximation. The quantitative constant is derived from radial orthogonality and an exact harmonic-number sum, with a standalone symbolic algebra audit.
scientific_limitations: Strict monotonicity and equality rigidity hold for all positive exponents. The explicit coefficient-sensitive derivative lower bound is proved only for 0<r<=2 and is not claimed optimal. The result applies to degree-n polynomials all of whose zeros lie on the unit circle, and the quantitative coefficient is stated after the standard self-inversive normalization.
title: Strict Baernstein monotonicity and quantitative binomial rigidity
